name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
title: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
answer: Sales tax, use tax, and value added tax are transaction taxes levied on goods and services, with sales tax charged at the point of sale, use tax owed on taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected, and VAT applied at each stage of production with credit for input tax. In AI accounting, this page covers how systems classify products and services, determine taxability, calculate rates, and prepare returns across jurisdictions. It also addresses exemption certificates, nexus rules, and cross-border VAT obligations.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Sales tax, use tax, and value added tax are transaction taxes levied on goods and services, with sales tax charged at the point of sale, use tax owed on taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected, and VAT applied at each stage of production with credit for input tax. In AI accounting, this page covers how systems classify products and services, determine taxability, calculate rates, and prepare returns across jurisdictions. It also addresses exemption certificates, nexus rules, and cross-border VAT obligations.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These systems run on cloud accounting platforms and ERP integrations that pull transaction data from invoices, ecommerce checkouts, and procurement records. They rely on tax content databases for rates, rules, and boundary files, plus APIs that connect to government filing systems. Processing is typically batch or near real time, with secure storage for transaction logs and audit trails.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by combining deterministic rule engines for known tax laws with machine learning models that classify products and services into tax categories from descriptions and spend data. Natural language processing reads invoices and contracts to extract line items, quantities, and jurisdictions. Anomaly detection flags unusual exemption claims or missing tax amounts before returns are filed.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on accuracy, auditability, and liability for underpayment or overpayment. Taxpayers remain responsible for returns even when software prepares them, so systems must preserve source documents and show how each tax decision was made. Data protection rules apply to customer and transaction records, and cross-border VAT reporting must follow local filing and invoice retention requirements. Provenance matters because tax authorities may ask for the exact rate version and rule set used on a given date.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: These tools are moving toward continuous transaction controls, where tax is calculated and reported to authorities in real time as invoices are issued. More jurisdictions are adopting e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements, which pushes AI systems to handle structured data exchange directly. The likely direction is fewer after-the-fact returns and more embedded, pre-approved tax decisions at the point of sale.
